chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed thirty dinars to emancipate a man from our companions with it, but he could not be found. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Buy (a slave) from the people, then emancipate him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if the specific slave named in a bequest for emancipation cannot be found?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *tadil* (substitution) in bequests, ruling that if the specific slave designated for emancipation is unavailable, the funds must be used to purchase a different slave to fulfill the testator's intent. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of preserving the *maqasid* (objectives) of the deceased by ensuring the charitable act is completed rather than left unfulfilled due to the absence of the specific individual. The ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh to adapt legal procedures to practical realities while maintaining the spiritual merit of the bequest.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Abu Hama who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about a man who bequeathed with thirty Dinars to emancipate (a slave) with it, a man from our companions. So that could not be found. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Buy (a slave) from the people, so emancipate him’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has narrated the following: “

I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who has made a will about thirty dinars to set free a man from our people but it cannot be done with that much. (The Imam) said, ‘A slave then must be bought from other people for this purpose.’”
